mistakes.question: The report includes ___ one-page summary for senior managers.
mistakes.explanation: Article choice follows pronunciation and whether the noun is specific, not simply the first written letter.

mistakes.question: The room contains new ___.
mistakes.explanation: A singular countable noun needs a determiner; use a/an according to sound. Information, equipment, advice and furniture are uncountable.

mistakes.question: The company opened ___ European branch last year.
mistakes.explanation: Use the for an identified noun or a second mention; uncountable nouns do not take a/an or a plural -s.

mistakes.question: I saw ___ advertisement for the course.
mistakes.explanation: A singular countable noun needs a determiner; use a/an according to sound. Information, equipment, advice and furniture are uncountable.

mistakes.question: There is ___ university near the branch.
mistakes.explanation: A singular countable noun needs a determiner; use a/an according to sound. Information, equipment, advice and furniture are uncountable.

mistakes.question: What time ___ the office close each day?
mistakes.explanation: Direct questions place the auxiliary before the subject; after do/does/did the main verb stays in its base form.

mistakes.question: The invoice has already ___ to the customer.
mistakes.explanation: When the subject receives the action, use be + past participle; the form of be carries the tense.

mistakes.question: The shop is going to ___ online payments next week.
mistakes.explanation: Will and be going to are followed by the base form; the present continuous can describe an arranged future event.

mistakes.question: The number of late deliveries ___ since the company changed its transport provider.
mistakes.explanation: A period continuing up to now requires the present perfect even when the sentence contains a past starting event.
